stem: Which statement best distinguishes pH from EC in irrigation water?
choices: pH describes acidity or basicity, while EC reflects overall dissolved-ion conductivity; neither measurement identifies complete water chemistry
pH estimates the concentration of every dissolved nutrient, while EC mainly reports water temperature and therefore adds little information about dissolved ions
pH and EC measure the same underlying property, so either value can substitute for the other when the meter is calibrated
EC directly measures alkalinity, so a stable EC value makes separate pH and alkalinity measurements largely unnecessary
rationale: pH and EC describe different properties. pH indicates acidity/basicity; EC is related to the total ionic concentration and does not identify individual ions or replace pH.
